To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the patient who is at risk of death from asthma has: 1) a history of asthma that is severe, with frequent attacks and hospitalizations, 2) an abnormal lung function, 3) a high bronchial reactivitiy, 4) a blunted hypoxic drive, and 5) a poor awareness of the seriousness of his disease.
asthma is an inflammatory disease that can lead to death and that many deaths are potentially preventable.

asthma deaths occur mainly in patients with severe asthma, and are preventable by early recognition of the disease and by early and aggressive therapy, including inhaled and oral steroids, with the goal of normalization of lung function and peak flow variability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the at-risk group and to develop a treatment plan that is effective and acceptable to patients.
understanding why some patients die from asthma and how to prevent these deaths.
identifying the patient at risk and the factors that contribute to the risk of dying.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the patient at risk can be identified, that the disease can be prevented and that the patient at high risk can be treated to prevent death.
we do know how to prevent fatal asthma, we just don't know how to do it.
asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease of the lung, which may lead to severe air flow obstruction and death if not adequately treated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
asthma deaths can be prevented, but the task of prevention is not easy.
asthma mortality has not been reduced in spite of the fact that the disease is better understood.
